label: Skilled bots' cron reader accepts only five-field cron or fixed macros, refuses anything else by name, never parses natural language, and outputs launchd calendar dictionaries rather than an internal schedule model.
OpenMausBot has a deterministic cron-to-preset parser covering every day, monthly day, monthly last day, yearly, weekdays, weekly and monthly-nth, plus a sentence renderer for a preset.
Rakazo has the reverse preset-to-cron function over the same vocabulary, plus presetFromCron and a round-trip test table that pins every preset form to its cron string.

Combining OpenMausBot's cron-to-preset parser with Rakazo's preset-to-cron function gives a deterministic sentence-to-cron bridge for a closed phrase set, with raw cron passthrough otherwise, mirroring OpenBot's form-versus-conversation split.
Event starts are a name-mapping problem, not NLP: a pull-request phrase maps to the existing git-hook trigger or a named queue, and an email phrase maps to a queue name a future mail connector feeds.

The current definition holds exactly one trigger object, and the installer and slot accounting both depend on it: the installer refuses a non-cron trigger and slot accounting refuses any schedule index past zero.

The smallest planner is a pure planRoutine(text) returning what, starts[], does and until from a phrase table, a trigger-name table, raw-cron passthrough and an explicit unparsed result; size M because the schema moves to a starts list and installer, slot accounting and status all read trigger.

A smaller v1 can keep the single-trigger invariant with one cron or one queue/git-hook start per routine, at size S, but it leaves OpenBot's multiple-starts gap open and is therefore a fallback rather than the recommended target.
